Diels–Alder reaction of butadiene and ethene

Author

Giovanni Gravili

Published

November 4, 2026

Modified

November 21, 2026

Abstract

Diels–Alder reaction of s-cis-1,3-butadiene and ethene to cyclohexene: which approach geometries reach the concerted transition state, and the reaction path and energies of the one that does.

Keywords

Diels–Alder, transition state, cyclohexene

NoteOngoing
  • The offset-plane saddle converged with one imaginary mode at 530.1194i\,\mathrm{cm}^{-1}, forming C–C bonds of 2.2675\,\text{\AA} and a stable closed-shell wavefunction.
  • Its IRC ends 76.6\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} below the saddle with the fragments apart and 246.0\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} below it with the ring closed, but neither end is a verified minimum.
  • The coplanar-guess workflow is rejected: it relaxed to a closed cyclohexene-like ring instead of the saddle.
  • The TS outcome map reached the saddle from 41 of its 90 starts, coplanar ones only with the methylene groups turned toward the closed ring’s twist.

Reaction

The parent Diels–Alder reaction closes the six-membered ring of cyclohexene in one concerted [4+2] step (Eq. 1, Fig. 2).

\ce{H2C=CH-CH=CH2 + H2C=CH2 -> C6H10} \tag{1}

  • The diene is s-cis-1,3-butadiene, \ce{C4H6}, with carbons \ce{C1} to \ce{C4}.
  • The dienophile is ethene, \ce{C2H4}, with carbons \ce{C5} and \ce{C6}.
  • The new bonds are \ce{C1-C6} and \ce{C4-C5}, of lengths r_{1,6} and r_{4,5}.
  • The terminal methylene groups of the diene sit at \ce{C1} and \ce{C4}.

Offset-plane path

  • The saddle has one imaginary mode, \tilde\nu=530.1194i\,\mathrm{cm}^{-1}, with r_{1,6}=2.2675\,\text{\AA} and r_{4,5}=2.2676\,\text{\AA}, and a stable closed-shell wavefunction.
  • Fig. 3 shows the reaction path along \pm s.
  • The reverse branch ends with the ring closed, \Delta E\approx246\,\mathrm{kJ}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1} below the saddle, which estimates the barrier to break the ring.
  • The forward branch ends with separated fragments, \Delta E\approx76\,\mathrm{kJ}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1} below the saddle, a lower bound because it stopped at its point limit.

Cyclohexene endpoint

  • The optimization from the reverse end converged to a boat ring, with r_{1,6}=1.5491\,\text{\AA} and r_{4,5}=1.5492\,\text{\AA}.
  • Its one imaginary mode, \tilde\nu=30.6556i\,\mathrm{cm}^{-1}, fails the minimum check, so the run is marked with caveats.
  • The mode moves the hydrogens of \ce{C5} and \ce{C6} and keeps the ring intact, as in a boat ring inversion.

Normal modes of the cyclohexene endpoint, animated, the imaginary mode first.

Coplanar guess

The coplanar guess puts both carbon skeletons in one plane, with the methylene groups turned by \tau=90^\circ.

  • Its optimization closed to a ring, with r_{1,6}=1.5482\,\text{\AA} and r_{4,5}=1.5498\,\text{\AA}, and one imaginary mode, \tilde\nu=33.3985i\,\mathrm{cm}^{-1}.
  • This mode is much softer than the saddle’s \tilde\nu=530.1194i\,\mathrm{cm}^{-1}, and the ring matches the boat ring-inversion saddle of cyclohexene.
  • The guess changed angle, distance and rotation together, so it does not isolate the cause.
  • The coplanar workflow is rejected.

Where the transition state is reached

Each start of the outcome map is one transition-state optimization from rigid fragments.

  • The distance r of the ethene centre from the midpoint of \ce{C5-C6} in the completed ring takes r\in\{1.29,1.70,2.55\}\,\text{\AA}.
  • The angle \theta of ethene from the diene plane runs from \theta=0^\circ, coplanar, to \theta=90^\circ, above the product bond.
  • The rotation \tau of the methylene groups about \ce{C1=C2} and \ce{C4=C3} takes \tau\in\{-45^\circ,-20^\circ,0^\circ,20^\circ,45^\circ,90^\circ\}.

The viewer below animates the optimization path of each start:

  • A start is chosen by method, r, \theta and \tau.
  • Its path runs from the initial geometry to the transition state where it converged.
  • Marked points give r and \theta at every frame.

Optimization path of each start of the outcome map, from the initial to the final geometry; r is measured from the pivot to the ethene centre and \theta from the diene plane.

The matrix below shows the outcome of every start (Tab. 1).

  • 41 of the 90 starts reached the verified saddle; the other 49 stopped at the optimizer’s step limit.
  • At \tau\in\{-45^\circ,-20^\circ,0^\circ\} no coplanar B3LYP start, at \theta=0^\circ, reaches it.
  • At \tau=45^\circ all three do, and at \tau\in\{20^\circ,90^\circ\} only the closest one, at r=1.29\,\text{\AA}, does.
  • The rotation therefore decides whether a coplanar start closes the ring, and \tau=45^\circ, the closed ring’s own twist, is the most productive rotation with 13 of 15 starts converged.

Orbital hypothesis

Two frontier pairs can bond, each only if its orbitals overlap:

  • The fragments are calculated alone at each start, at B3LYP/6\text{-}31\mathrm{G}(d,p) in PySCF in Gaussian’s form, B3LYPG.
  • They therefore lack polarization by the partner.
  • The path notebook adds it through the complex.
  • The names normal and inverse demand follow the dienophile, which is the electron-poor acceptor in normal demand and the donor in inverse demand.
  • Without substituents both pairs take part.
  • Symmetry labels are those of the saddle’s point group, C_{s}; each pair’s donor and acceptor share one.
  • The viewer shows the product whose integral is S, and its toggle the product whose integral is S' and the sum \psi_\mathrm{HOMO}(\ce{C4H6})+\psi_\mathrm{LUMO}(\ce{C2H4}):

f=\psi_\mathrm{HOMO}(\ce{C4H6})\,\psi_\mathrm{LUMO}(\ce{C2H4}),\qquad f'=\psi_\mathrm{HOMO}(\ce{C2H4})\,\psi_\mathrm{LUMO}(\ce{C4H6}),\qquad S=\int f\,\mathrm{d}V

  • Signs make S,S'>0; each surface of f or f' encloses a share \eta=90\% of \int|f|\,\mathrm{d}V or \int|f'|\,\mathrm{d}V.

Frontier-pair products and sum on the starting geometry of each B3LYP start, with the forming bonds measured.

Across the B3LYP starts S mostly grows as \theta rises and as ethene comes closer, and vanishes at \tau=90^\circ, with these exceptions:

  • It does not rise with \theta at \tau=-45^\circ.
  • It does not fall with r at \theta=60^\circ for \tau\in\{-45^\circ,-20^\circ\}.
  • It does not fall with r at \theta=90^\circ for \tau\in\{-45^\circ,-20^\circ,0^\circ,20^\circ\}.
  • S rises with \theta at every distance.
  • It falls as r grows, except at \theta=90^\circ, where r=1.70\,\text{\AA} gives a larger S than r=1.29\,\text{\AA}.
  • S, S' and the initial forming bond separate the outcomes with areas under the ROC curve A_\mathrm{ROC}=0.87, 0.91 and 0.84, the chance that a start that reached the saddle has the larger value; A_\mathrm{ROC}=0.5 is chance. They rank this optimizer’s outcomes, not the surface.
  • From \tau=-20^\circ to \tau=45^\circ the starts that reached the saddle have the larger mean overlap, \bar S=0.14 against 0.04 at \tau=0^\circ.
  • Frontier overlap at the start is not needed, since at \tau=90^\circ both S and S' vanish, yet 4 starts reached the saddle.
  • A crowded start, such as hydrogens facing each other, is a high-energy point the optimizer relaxes away, not a barrier.
  • The saddle belongs to the surface, since every converged start reached it, with energies within \lvert\Delta E\rvert<0.1\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}.
  • A failed start therefore shows only that the optimizer missed it.

Atom pairs and the Klopman–Salem term

Each overlap splits into atom pairs (A,B), one atom of each fragment, c_\mu and d_\nu being the donor and acceptor coefficients; the plot sums them by group G, and S' alike:

S=\sum_{A\in\ce{C4H6}}\sum_{B\in\ce{C2H4}}S_{A,B},\qquad S_{A,B}=\sum_{\mu\in A}\sum_{\nu\in B}c_\mu d_\nu\langle\phi_\mu|\phi_\nu\rangle,\qquad S_G=\sum_{(A,B)\in G}S_{A,B}

  • Primary carbons are pairs that form the bonds \ce{C1-C6} and \ce{C4-C5}.
  • Terminal carbons are pairs of reacting atoms that do not bond to each other.
  • Secondary carbons are pairs with \ce{C2} or \ce{C3}, which do not react.
  • Hydrogens are pairs with a hydrogen, which does not react.

The Klopman–Salem equation turns both overlaps into one frontier stabilization, with k an unknown constant:

\Delta E\approx-2k^2F,\qquad F=\frac{S^2}{\Delta\epsilon}+\frac{S'^2}{\Delta\epsilon'} \tag{2}

\Delta\epsilon=\epsilon_\mathrm{LUMO}(\ce{C2H4})-\epsilon_\mathrm{HOMO}(\ce{C4H6}),\qquad \Delta\epsilon'=\epsilon_\mathrm{LUMO}(\ce{C4H6})-\epsilon_\mathrm{HOMO}(\ce{C2H4})

Future calculations

Three prepared calculations would tell the strain of the starts, the surface and the optimizer apart.

Calculation Goal Measured outcome
Single points of the 72 distinct starts Tell whether the failures are the strained starts Start energy E-E_{\mathrm{TS}}, plotted against the outcome
Relaxed scan of both forming bonds from \theta=90^\circ at \tau\in\{0^\circ,45^\circ\} Tell one surface from a higher barrier on every path, which would be sterics E(r) and \tau(r) of both scans
Larger step limit for the 49 failures Separate the optimizer from the surface Share of the failures that reach the saddle, plotted against the step limit

Conclusions

  • The offset-plane saddle leads to cyclohexene, which shows the ring forming at this level of theory.
  • A coplanar start with untwisted methylene groups does not reach the saddle, while the same start rotated toward the closed ring’s twist does; the rotation, not coplanarity, drives the coplanar guess to the ring.
  • Breaking the ring takes \Delta E\approx246\,\mathrm{kJ}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1} up to the saddle, pending a verified product minimum.
  • The reactant energy, the forward barrier and the reaction energy need a verified reactant reference.
  • A non-converged start shows only where this optimizer stops within its step limit, so the map describes the optimizer’s behaviour, not the surface.

NoteOngoing
  • The saddle refinement converged to a first-order saddle with one imaginary mode at 530.1194i\,\mathrm{cm}^{-1}, forming C–C bonds of 2.2675\,\text{\AA} and a stable closed-shell wavefunction.
  • The IRC branches ran along \pm s, ending 76.6\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} below the saddle with the fragments separated and 246.0\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} below it with the ring closed.
  • The reverse terminus converged to a boat-shaped cyclohexene with one 30.6556i\,\mathrm{cm}^{-1} mode, not a minimum, and the forward-terminus reactant optimization stopped at its 100-step limit with the fragments drifting apart, so neither endpoint is a verified minimum.
  • Variant of the coplanar-guess workflow.
